Without a Stripe secret key this endpoint cannot produce a result; do not call it.

usage.guide: POST to the URL with a JSON body {phone, message} where phone is E.164 format (+countrycode...) and message is the SMS text. The response is HTTP 200 regardless of outcome - read body.success: true means the SMS was sent (body.textId is the message id), false means it failed (body.error explains why). This sends a real text message, so confirm the recipient before calling.

entries.name: Laso Finance Auth
entries.description: Obtain Laso Finance auth credentials by proving wallet ownership (SIWX / CAIP-122). Returns a 1h Firebase id_token used as a Bearer token for every other Laso endpoint, plus a refresh_token, the callable_base_url, and your user_id (lowercase wallet address). This is the required first step before any read (search-merchants, get-card-data) or before reading card details after ordering.

usage.callShape: GET https://laso.finance/auth — free, no x402 payment. Authenticated via SIWX: send a base64-encoded CAIP-122 SIGN-IN-WITH-X header proving wallet ownership (agentcash fetch handles this automatically). No query params, no body.
usage.outputShape: auth.id_token, auth.refresh_token, auth.expires_in (seconds, e.g. '3600'), callable_base_url, user_id
quirks: FREE / SIWX-only: no x402 payment, just a wallet signature (agentcash fetch supplies the SIGN-IN-WITH-X header).
auth.id_token is a 1h Firebase JWT. Use it as `Authorization: Bearer <id_token>` for ALL other Laso endpoints — they 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' without it.
agentcash fetch does NOT auto-attach the Bearer token to subsequent calls — you must capture id_token here and pass it manually in the Authorization header.
Renew with POST /auth (grant_type=refresh_token) using auth.refresh_token before the token expires.
user_id is your lowercase wallet address; all card/balance data is scoped to this identity.
The paid card-ordering endpoints (/get-card, /order-intl-card) ALSO return fresh auth credentials, so you never need to pay just to get a token.

entries.name: Laso Finance Merchant Acceptance Search
entries.description: Search Laso's crowdsourced merchant database to check whether a Laso prepaid card is accepted at a given merchant before relying on it. Returns matching merchants with an acceptance status (accepted / not_accepted / unknown), website URL, description, and usage notes.

usage.callShape: GET https://laso.finance/search-merchants?q=<merchant>&card_type=<Non-Reloadable U.S.|Non-Reloadable International> — query params in URL, no body. Requires header `Authorization: Bearer <id_token from /auth>`. card_type optional (defaults to 'Non-Reloadable U.S.').
usage.outputShape: merchants[].{name, url, status('accepted'|'not_accepted'|'unknown'), description, notes}, query, count, card_type, note
quirks: FREE read, but REQUIRES `Authorization: Bearer <id_token>` from GET /auth first — returns 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' otherwise (agentcash fetch does not attach it automatically).
Required query param `q` = merchant name (e.g. 'amazon', 'netflix').
card_type enum is exactly 'Non-Reloadable U.S.' or 'Non-Reloadable International' (note the trailing period and capitalization); defaults to 'Non-Reloadable U.S.'.
status='unknown' does NOT mean the card will fail — the DB only covers merchants users have previously tried (see the `note` field). Returns many fuzzy matches (37 for 'amazon').
Some merchants carry `notes` advising indirect use (e.g. load funds via Amazon Reload, then spend from the Amazon balance).

entries.name: Laso Finance Get Card Data
entries.description: Retrieve details for the caller's Laso prepaid card(s). With a card_id, returns that single card including the card number, CVV, and expiry once status is 'ready' (US) / 'complete' (intl). Without card_id, lists all of the caller's cards of a given card_type. This is the polling endpoint to fetch the actual card credentials after ordering via /get-card or /order-intl-card.

usage.callShape: GET https://laso.finance/get-card-data?card_id=<id>&card_type=<...> — all params optional, no body. Requires header `Authorization: Bearer <id_token from /auth>`. Omit card_id to list all cards (returns {cards:[...]}); pass card_id to get one card (returns the single-card object).
usage.outputShape: List mode: cards[].{card_id, card_type, usd_amount, status, country?, card_details?{card_number,exp_month,exp_year,cvv,available_balance}, transactions[]}. Single mode (with card_id): same fields at top level, no `cards` wrapper.
quirks: FREE read, but REQUIRES `Authorization: Bearer <id_token>` from GET /auth first — 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' otherwise (agentcash fetch does not attach it automatically).
Response is polymorphic: NO card_id -> {cards:[...]} array; WITH card_id -> a single card object (no `cards` wrapper).

card_details (card_number/cvv/expiry/available_balance) is only present when status='ready' (US) or 'complete' (international); freshly ordered cards return status='pending'/'queued' with no details — poll until ready.
card_type filter (list mode) defaults to 'Non-Reloadable U.S.'; pass 'Non-Reloadable International' to see intl cards.

International cards carry extra fields (label, charged_usd_amount, fees_paid, state, queued_order_card_id) and a different transaction shape (merchant/status vs is_credit). After intl admin fulfillment the card is reissued with a new card_id; querying the ORIGINAL card_id still resolves via queued_order_card_id.
Empty result for a wallet with no cards is {cards:[]} (verified).

entries.name: Laso Finance Order USA Prepaid Card
entries.description: Create and fund a real US-issued USD prepaid debit card. The x402 payment EQUALS the card value: amount=5 charges 5 USDC on Base/Solana and loads a $5 card (min $5, max $1000). Returns a card_id with status='pending'; poll /get-card-data with the id_token to retrieve the card number/CVV/expiry once ready.

usage.callShape: GET https://laso.finance/get-card?amount=5&format=json — x402-paid (the charge = the amount). amount required (number 5-1000). format optional: 'json' (default, agent-friendly) or 'html' (browser redirect page). No Bearer token needed for this call — the x402 payment authenticates + identifies you, and the response itself returns fresh auth credentials.
usage.outputShape: auth.{id_token,refresh_token,expires_in}, callable_base_url, user_id, card.{card_id, usd_amount, country('US'), timestamp, timestamp_readable, status('pending')}
quirks: NOT CALLED (outward / irreversible): this provisions a REAL funded US debit card with REAL money. The x402 charge equals the card value, so amount=5 actually spends $5 (5000000 base units USDC), amount=1000 spends $1000. Requires deliberate human approval.
THE PRICE IS THE PRODUCT: there is no flat fee — the registry's $5 is the MINIMUM card value, not a service fee. Pricing is dynamic 5-1000 USD.
Pass &format=json so an agent gets JSON; default mimeType is text/html (browser redirect view).

Card returns status='pending' with a card_id (e.g. O-01KTN62...). The card number/CVV/expiry are NOT in this response — poll GET /get-card-data?card_id=<id> using the returned auth.id_token as Bearer token.
US-ONLY: USD card, US merchants only, physical goods must ship to a US address. For non-US use /order-intl-card instead.
Prepaid cards are not accepted at all merchants — check GET /search-merchants first.
Card + token are bound to the paying wallet (user_id); no separate SIWX/sign-in needed for this paid call.

VERIFIED via prior purchase 2026-06-08 (MASTERKEY_ASSETS.md): bought card_id O-01KTN62GBAKT1VERAFMC962NYN, $5 US balance. GET laso.finance/get-card?amount=N — the amount is the card VALUE loaded (recoverable), NOT a fee. Outward/irreversible (real money onto a real card) → needsApproval.

entries.name: StableGiftCards Search
entries.description: Search the Bitrefill catalog (1,500+ gift-card, top-up, and eSIM brands across 180+ countries) by name, country, type, or category. SIWX-gated and FREE (no USDC charged).

usage.callShape: POST https://stablegiftcards.dev/api/search with JSON body {query, country?, product_type?, category?, in_stock?, page?, per_page?} + SIWX wallet signature (no x402 payment). 'query' defaults to '*'. 'country' must be uppercase ISO Alpha-2 (US, IT, BR). 'product_type' enum: 'giftcard' | 'esim'. 'per_page' max 500 (default 25).

quirks: Auth is SIWX, NOT x402 — returns the SIWX challenge until signed; once signed it is FREE (no USDC). Use --siwx.

packages[].id is product-prefixed with a '<&>' delimiter, e.g. 'netflix-usa<&>30'. For buying, /api/buy wants the bare packages[].value ('30'), NOT this id.
packages[].price is an internal minor unit (e.g. 48643 for a $30 card); packages[].amount is the real human value (30).
country must be UPPERCASE 2-letter ISO; lowercase or 3-letter is rejected.
Returns 'range' instead of fixed 'packages' for variable-amount products.
SIWX free read (no payment) — verified 2026-06-11.

For phone top-ups include phone_number on the item. Output: {invoice_id, tx_hash, amount_usdc, orders[].{product_id, product_name, value, status, code?, pin?, link?}}

entries.name: Greeneris BIC Validator
entries.description: Validate a BIC/SWIFT code offline (ISO 9362 structure — 4-letter bank, 2-letter country, 2-char location, optional 3-char branch — plus a real ISO 3166-1 country-code check), returning validity, the parsed parts and whether it is a test BIC.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/bic?bic=BNPAFRPP (BIC/SWIFT code as the `bic` query param, 8 or 11 chars). x402 paid endpoint (~0.001 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { bic, valid (bool), bank_code, country (ISO2), location, branch (nullable), is_test_bic (bool), source } }. On an invalid BIC the data object carries valid:false with the parsed parts it could recover.
quirks: Pure offline deterministic computation (ISO 9362 structure check + ISO 3166-1 country table); NO SWIFT-directory existence lookup, so it confirms the code is well-formed and the country code is real, not that the bank/branch actually exists. Provider states a 1-year cache.
The BIC MUST be passed as the `bic` query param; accepts both 8-char (BNPAFRPP) and 11-char (DEUTDEFF500) forms.
is_test_bic flags a test BIC (8th character '0').
Pairs with /v1/validate/iban on the same host for BIC/IBAN country-consistency checks.
Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling validators (IBAN, LEI, ISIN, email) and EU registry lookups live on the same host as separate operations.
usage.guide: Call GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/bic with the BIC/SWIFT code in the `bic` query param, e.g. ?bic=BNPAFRPP (8-char) or ?bic=DEUTDEFF500 (11-char). It is an x402 paid endpoint (~0.001 USDC on Base, no API key); pay the 402 quote and re-request. The JSON response is { ok, data: { bic, valid, bank_code, country, location, branch, is_test_bic, source } } — check data.valid. Validation is offline structure + ISO country-code check only, not a SWIFT-directory existence lookup.

entries.name: Greeneris IBAN Validator

queryParams.iban: IBAN to validate (spaces and dashes allowed) — required

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/iban?iban=FR1420041010050500013M02606 (IBAN as the `iban` query param; spaces/dashes tolerated). x402 paid endpoint (~0.001 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { iban, valid (bool), country (ISO2), check_digits, bban, source } }. On an invalid IBAN the data object carries valid:false plus a precise failure reason instead.
quirks: Pure offline deterministic computation (ISO 13616 format + per-country SWIFT-registry length + ISO 7064 mod-97 checksum); provider states a 1-year cache. No live bank-account existence check — checksum/format only.
The IBAN MUST be passed as the `iban` query param; spaces and dashes in the value are tolerated.
Covers ~85 countries per the public SWIFT registry.
Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling validators (BIC, LEI, ISIN, email) and EU registry lookups live on the same host as separate operations.
usage.guide: Call GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/iban with the IBAN in the `iban` query param, e.g. ?iban=FR1420041010050500013M02606 (spaces/dashes allowed). It is an x402 paid endpoint (~0.001 USDC on Base, no API key); pay the 402 quote and re-request. The JSON response is { ok, data: { iban, valid, country, check_digits, bban, source } } — check data.valid; validation is offline checksum/format only, not a bank-account existence lookup.

entries.name: 24kLabs IBAN + BIC Validator
entries.description: Validate an IBAN (ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum with per-country length rules) together with a SWIFT/BIC code (ISO 9362 structure), returning validity plus extracted country, check digits, BBAN, and BIC bank/country/location/branch parts.

body.iban: string — the IBAN to validate (spaces tolerated) — required
body.bic: string — the SWIFT/BIC code to validate — required

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/iban-bic-validate with JSON body {"iban":"GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32","bic":"DEUTDEFF"}. Pure x402 paid endpoint (0.002 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request; the result is returned inline in the 200 response.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { service, result: { iban_input, country (ISO2 from IBAN), iban_valid (bool), iban_formatted, check_digits, bban, bic_valid (bool), bic_bank_code, bic_country (ISO2 from BIC), bic_location, bic_branch }, latency_ms }. Verified response for {iban:'GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32', bic:'DEUTDEFF'}: { service:'iban-bic-validate', result:{ country:'GB', iban_valid:true, check_digits:'82', bban:'WEST12345698765432', bic_valid:true, bic_bank_code:'DEUT', bic_country:'DE', bic_location:'FF', bic_branch:'primary office' }, latency_ms:0 }.
quirks: Validates IBAN and BIC together — provide both `iban` and `bic` in the body. Spaces in the IBAN are tolerated and echoed back in iban_formatted.

Offline deterministic validation (IBAN ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum + per-country length; SWIFT/BIC ISO 9362 structure with country-code check) — format/checksum only, NOT a live bank-account or SWIFT-network existence check.
IBAN country and BIC country are reported separately (an IBAN can be GB while the BIC resolves to DE, as in the verified example) — the endpoint does not assert they match.

Distinct from the sibling 24kLabs IBAN / ABA / SWIFT / Card Validator (single auto-detecting `value` field) and the Greeneris BIC Validator (BIC only) — this one takes explicit iban+bic fields and returns both results.
Part of the broad 24kLabs pay-per-call developer/finance toolkit on api.24klabs.ai.
usage.guide: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/iban-bic-validate with JSON body {"iban":"<iban>","bic":"<swift/bic>"}. It is a pure x402 paid endpoint (0.002 USDC on Base, no API key); pay the 402 quote and re-request. The 200 response returns { service, result:{ iban_valid, country, check_digits, bban, bic_valid, bic_bank_code, bic_country, bic_location, bic_branch }, latency_ms } — check result.iban_valid and result.bic_valid. Validation is offline checksum/format only, not a live account or SWIFT-network lookup.

It is a pure x402 paid endpoint (0.002 USDC on Base, no API key); pay the 402 quote and re-request. entries.name: Agentstools BIC Lookup
entries.description: Reverse BIC/SWIFT lookup: given a BIC, return the resolved bank name(s), the country and the domestic bank codes, from offline open-registry data (schwifty, MIT) — no network or API keys.

queryParams.bic: 8- or 11-character BIC/SWIFT code, e.g. COBADEFFXXX — required

outputSchema.error_type: string|null (null on success; set on a malformed BIC)
outputSchema.bank_names: string[] (all bank/branch names registered under this BIC)
outputSchema.domestic_bank_codes: string[] (national bank/sort codes mapped to this BIC)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bank/bic?bic=COBADEFFXXX (BIC/SWIFT code as the `bic` query param, 8 or 11 chars; `swift` accepted as an alias). Pure x402 paid endpoint (0.005 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request; the result is returned inline in the 200 response.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { valid (bool), bic, error_type (null on success), bank_names (string[] — e.g. ['Commerzbank', 'Commerzbank Bamberg', ...]), country: { name, alpha_2 (ISO2), alpha_3 (ISO3), numeric }, domestic_bank_codes (string[]), disclaimer }. Verified for COBADEFFXXX → valid:true, ~63 Commerzbank name variants, country Germany (DE/DEU/276), ~200 domestic bank codes.
quirks: Pure offline deterministic lookup against open registries (schwifty, MIT) — no live network call, no API key.
A single BIC can map to many bank_names (one per registered branch/GF unit) and many domestic_bank_codes — the Commerzbank COBADEFFXXX example returns dozens of each.
A malformed BIC returns valid:false with an error_type, never a 500.
NOT KYC / Confirmation-of-Payee — it resolves registry metadata only, does not prove the account exists or belongs to anyone (see the response disclaimer).
usage.guide: Look up who owns a BIC/SWIFT code. Call GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bank/bic with the BIC in the `bic` query param (e.g. ?bic=COBADEFFXXX). It is an x402-paid GET (0.005 USDC on Base, no key): the first request returns HTTP 402 with a payment-required quote; pay it and re-request to get the 200 JSON with the resolved bank name(s), country and domestic bank codes. Use it to attach a human-readable bank name/country to a BIC before a payment or for reconciliation; pair with bank/validate or bank/verify for IBAN checks. Not a fraud/KYC verdict.

entries.name: Agentstools Bank Validate
entries.description: Validate an IBAN offline (ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum + per-country structure/length via the schwifty MIT registry), returning validity, the resolved country, the BBAN/IBAN format spec, and on rejection a granular error_type (invalid_checksum, invalid_length, invalid_structure, invalid_country).

iban.description: IBAN to validate (spaces optional, any case).

valid.description: True if the IBAN passes the ISO 13616 checksum and per-country structure/length.

error_type.description: null when valid; on rejection one of invalid_checksum, invalid_length, invalid_structure, invalid_country.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bank/validate?iban=<IBAN> (IBAN in the `iban` query param; spaces optional, any case). No request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: valid (bool), iban (echoed input), error_type (null when valid; else invalid_checksum|invalid_length|invalid_structure|invalid_country), country {name, alpha_2, alpha_3, numeric}, format_spec {bban_spec, bban_length, iban_length}, disclaimer. Verified paid 200 for iban=DE89370400440532013000: { valid:true, iban:'DE89370400440532013000', error_type:null, country:{ name:'Germany', alpha_2:'DE', alpha_3:'DEU', numeric:'276' }, format_spec:{ bban_spec:'8!n10!n', bban_length:18, iban_length:22 }, disclaimer:'...' }.
quirks: Pass the IBAN as the `iban` query param; spaces are optional and case is ignored.

OFFLINE structural validation only (ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum + per-country structure/length via the schwifty MIT registry) — it does NOT prove the account exists or belongs to anyone; no Confirmation-of-Payee / account-holder name matching, no bank/SEPA network call, no KYC. NOT legal or fraud advice; show the disclaimer.
On an invalid IBAN the 200 body carries valid:false plus a granular error_type (invalid_checksum, invalid_length, invalid_structure, invalid_country) instead of a null error_type.
The provider positions this as the 'cheap-first' route before the fuller /bank/verify fusion endpoint (account-existence + risk indicators) on the same host; /bank/bic is a separate BIC lookup.
The input IBAN is not stored or logged per the provider disclaimer.
usage.guide: Validate an IBAN's structure in one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bank/validate?iban=<IBAN> (spaces optional, any case), e.g. ?iban=DE89370400440532013000. Synchronous — the 200 body returns { valid, iban, error_type, country{name,alpha_2,alpha_3,numeric}, format_spec{bban_spec,bban_length,iban_length}, disclaimer }. Check `valid`; on rejection read `error_type` (invalid_checksum|invalid_length|invalid_structure|invalid_country). This is OFFLINE ISO 13616 checksum + per-country format validation (schwifty, MIT) — it does not confirm the account exists or its owner, and is not KYC/legal advice. Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), no API key or account.

entries.name: Agentstools Bank Verify
entries.description: Verify a bank account / IBAN in one keyless call — ISO 13616 checksum + per-country structure validation, BIC / bank name / branch resolution, country details, SEPA-zone flag, and a deterministic 0-100 fraud/KYC risk score with band, reasons and weighted signals, all computed offline from open-registry data.

iban.description: REQUIRED. IBAN to verify (spaces optional, any case), e.g. DE89370400440532013000.

expected_country.description: Optional ISO-3166 alpha-2 country the account is expected in (e.g. DE); a mismatch raises the risk score.

valid.description: Structural validity (ISO 13616 checksum + per-country BBAN structure).

bank_sanctions_advisory.description: ADVISORY-ONLY fuzzy name match of the resolved bank name against a public sanctions list: {potential_match, matched_name, list, programs[], score, advisory}. NOT a confirmation.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bank/verify with query params: iban=<IBAN, required> plus optional expected_country=<ISO-3166 alpha-2> (alias: country). No request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: valid (bool, structural ISO 13616 + BBAN validity), iban, error_type, country {name,alpha_2,alpha_3,numeric}, format_spec {bban_spec,bban_length,iban_length}, bic, bank_name, branch_code, bank_code, in_sepa_zone (bool), expected_country, risk_score (0-100), risk_band (low|medium|high), reasons[], signals[] {signal,dimension,severity,weight}, high_risk_jurisdiction, virtual_iban_issuer, bank_sanctions_advisory {potential_match,matched_name,list,programs[],score,advisory}, disclaimer. Live paid 200 for iban=DE89370400440532013000&expected_country=DE returned valid=true, country Germany, bic 'COBADEFFXXX', bank_name 'Commerzbank', bank_code '37040044', in_sepa_zone=true, risk_score 0, risk_band 'low'. Note: the run surfaced a bank_sanctions_advisory potential_match (matched_name 'Ocean Maritime Management Company, Limited', list 'EU') with weight 0 — an ADVISORY-ONLY fuzzy name coincidence, not a real sanctions hit on Commerzbank.
quirks: `iban` is the only required query param; `expected_country` (alias `country`) is optional ISO-3166 alpha-2 — a mismatch against the IBAN's country raises the risk score.

Fully OFFLINE: computed from schwifty (MIT) open-registry data — no paid bank/HLR API is resold. BIC/bank-name/branch resolution covers ~45 countries (all SEPA plus UA/CH/NO/DK etc.); structural validity covers 127 countries.
Structural + resolution + risk INDICATORS ONLY. Does NOT prove the account exists or belongs to any person/company — no Confirmation-of-Payee / account-holder name matching. Not legal/KYC advice.

bank_sanctions_advisory is a fuzzy name match with weight 0 (advisory) — treat as a lead to verify against the official list, not a verdict; the German test IBAN produced a benign false-positive advisory match.
Use ONLY public test IBANs (e.g. DE89370400440532013000) or provider examples when testing — never real PII. Input IBAN is not stored or logged. Invalid input returns a 4xx, never a 500.
usage.guide: Verify a bank account / IBAN in one keyless x402 call — for fraud, KYC/AML, payout and supplier-onboarding loops. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bank/verify?iban=<IBAN> (spaces optional, any case), optionally &expected_country=<ISO-3166 alpha-2> to flag a country mismatch. Synchronous — the 200 body carries: structural validity (ISO 13616 checksum + per-country BBAN structure), the parsed country and format_spec, the resolved bic/bank_name/branch_code/bank_code (open bank-registry coverage ~45 countries), the SEPA-zone flag, and a deterministic risk_score (0-100) with a low/medium/high band, human-readable reasons[] and weighted signals[] you can re-rank with your own policy. Computed entirely offline from schwifty (MIT) — no paid bank API resold, input not stored. These are risk INDICATORS, NOT a definitive fraud verdict; the result does NOT prove the account exists or who owns it (no name matching), and any bank-name sanctions match is ADVISORY ONLY. Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), no API key or account. Use public test IBANs only when testing.
